target.name: Parallel Systems
target.founder: Matt Soule, John Howard, Ben Stabler

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Parallel Systems is a Series B transportation company that has raised $100M to date. The broader transportation sector contains 7 private peers at various stages, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and DeepDrive; no public comparables exist in a sufficiently narrow peer set.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within transportation—only 3 same-sector companies exist, but none met the filters for a statistically reliable median. Stage-progression methodology was therefore the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($100M) as a proxy base value of $25M and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $48M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $40M (low) to $55M (high), centered at $48M. This range reflects uncertainty around both the proxy base (early-stage valuation estimates remain noisy) and the generalized step-up multiplier, which may not capture Parallel Systems' specific risk profile or market conditions. The single-method foundation underscores the need for additional data—particularly same-stage transportation comparables or revenue/unit-economics if available—to narrow the band and reduce reliance on stage-based mechanics alone.
